scenes.prompt:
Layered paper diorama photographed as a miniature set: thick textured watercolour paper, translucent vellum water layers, warm LED backlight, deep navy and white paper with glowing neon-orange accents, soft cast shadows between layers, shallow depth of field, macro lens.
Top third: THE PENGUIN from the reference sheet, rendered as a paper-craft character: small round egg-shaped penguin, black head and back, white belly, big white eye-rings, small dark beak with an orange tip, oversized orange feet, three thin feathers sticking up from its head. It wears a tiny yellow hard hat, standing on a small floating paper ice floe at night, peering down into the water. Below the waterline, translucent vellum layers of ocean fall away into darkness; far below, a thin cable glows orange on the seabed. Foreground: a paper wave edge. Lots of depth.

It wears a tiny brass diving helmet over its head feathers and has just landed beside the cable, puffs of paper sand around its feet. Paper kelp in the foreground, layered dark water above.

voices.label: A. Calm deadpan explainer (Charon)
voices.prompt:
# AUDIO PROFILE: Curious Penguin narrator
### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: Calm, matter-of-fact, slightly deadpan narrator of a viral 3D-animated explainer Short. Quick but unhurried, even energy, never hyped. Let the facts be the surprise. Tiny pauses before reveals, a dry hint of a smirk. Cool, nonchalant, curious.
Pace: around 165 to 175 words a minute, Shorts pacing.
#### TRANSCRIPT
Your messages don't fly through space. [short pause] They crawl along the bottom of the ocean. About ninety-five percent of the data between continents runs through cables no thicker than a garden hose. And they break. A lot. Around a hundred and fifty times a year. Fishing gear, ship anchors. [short pause] Occasionally, a shark. So what if every cable snapped at once?
